draft.title: Networks, vertices and edges
card: A network shows connections. Each point is a vertex, and each line joining two vertices is an edge. Towns joined by roads make a network: the towns are vertices and the roads are edges.
the degree of a vertex is the number of edges that meet at it. Count the edges touching the vertex.
Example: a network has vertices P, Q, R and S. The edges are PQ, PR, PS and QR. P meets three edges, so its degree is 3. S meets only PS, so its degree is 1.
Add up all the degrees and you get twice the number of edges, because every edge has two ends. Here the degrees are 3, 2, 2 and 1, which total 8, and there are 4 edges.
draft.remember: Vertices are points, edges are lines, and degree counts the edges at a vertex.

a.q: A network has vertices A, B, C and D. Its edges are AB, AC, AD and BC. What is the degree of vertex A?
a.why: Three edges meet at A: AB, AC and AD. The edge BC does not touch A, so it is not counted. Counting all 4 edges would give the number of edges, not the degree of A.
a.clue: Count only the edges that have A as an end.

b.q: A network of walking tracks has 6 edges. What is the total of the degrees of all its vertices?
b.why: Every edge has two ends, so each edge adds 2 to the total of the degrees. 6 × 2 = 12. A total of 6 would count each edge only once.
b.clue: Each edge has two ends, and each end adds to a degree.

check.summary: No problems found. The card's example degrees (3, 2, 2, 1, totalling 8 for 4 edges) check out, and both questions have a single correct answer (3 and 12) that matches the explanations.
